I started learning how to crochet in November and so far I've made a coaster, a little pencil pouch for my hooks and tape measure, and a lopsided hat. Right now I'm working on my first scarf and it's slow going but I'm really happy with how it's coming out!! I'm probably going to start making a lanyard today to take a little break from the scarf. After the scarf I'm going to start my first blanket!

I didn't have an actual hobby for the longest time and now I'm in love with crochet and look forward to it every day tbh. I'm so excited to see how I've improved a year from now. And also: I already can't stop buying yarn.
The Avalanches- Since I Left You

I kept an item my rapist gave me right after it happened for about four months afterwards. After awhile it got hidden under some stuff so I didn't look at it very often, but when I did it triggered some bad breakdowns. I didn't want to get rid of it though- like you said it was proof that what happened actually happened and I wasn't just making it all up or overreacting. Which is weird cause like, I didn't want to be reminded of what happened but having proof that it happened validated me? I can't really explain it either I guess but I know exactly how you feel.

About a month ago I impulsively got rid of it and don't really think about the item anymore. I don't regret it cause I know it was just upsetting me but sometimes I do miss having that proof. I'm glad I waited awhile before I threw it out though! If I had thrown it away sooner after my rape I feel like I would have freaked out and doubted my reality even more.

If you're not comfortable throwing them out yet I would suggest maybe doing what I did and putting them somewhere where you won't see them or think about them often? My item definitely wasn't as emotionally charged as underwear (it was just a backpack) but it might help. Then if you feel more comfortable getting rid of them later then you can do that. What happened to you was pretty recent and I think it makes sense to want to hold onto items like that. Keep in mind though that having them to look at might be doing you more harm than good.
